items.question: Should an NBFC obtain third‑party assessments and market input on a service provider, and verify that the provider’s systems are compatible with the NBFC’s and meet acceptable performance standards such as customer service?
items.answer:

- Where possible, an NBFC shall obtain independent reviews and market feedback on the service provider to supplement its own due‑diligence findings[S1].  
- The NBFC shall also evaluate whether the service provider’s systems are compatible with those of the NBFC and whether the provider’s performance standards—including customer service—are acceptable[S1].

items.question: क्या नियंत्रण परिवर्तन के लिए सार्वजनिक नोटिस प्रकाशित करने से पहले RBI की अनुमति आवश्यक है, और नोटिस में किन विवरणों को शामिल करना चाहिए?
items.answer:
**हाँ**, नियंत्रण परिवर्तन के लिए सार्वजनिक नोटिस प्रकाशित करने से पहले RBI की पूर्व अनुमति आवश्यक है।  

- सार्वजनिक नोटिस को **RBI की पूर्व अनुमति प्राप्त करने के बाद** NBFC तथा ट्रांसफ़ीeree पक्ष (या दोनों मिलकर) देना होगा[S1]।  
- नोटिस में निम्नलिखित विवरण शामिल होने चाहिए:  
  1. **विक्री या नियंत्रण‑स्थानांतरण की इच्छा** का संकेत[S1]।  
  2. **ट्रांसफ़ीeree की जानकारी** (परिचय)[S1]।  
  3. **विक्री/स्थानांतरण के कारण**[S1]।  

इसके अतिरिक्त, नोटिस कम से कम एक प्रमुख राष्ट्रीय तथा एक प्रमुख स्थानीय (पंजीकृत कार्यालय के स्थान को कवर करने वाले) भाषा के समाचारपत्र में, प्रभावी होने से **30 दिन पहले** प्रकाशित किया जाना चाहिए[S2]।

items.question: Which amalgamation scenarios are covered by the RBI Voluntary Amalgamation Directions for NBFCs?
items.answer:
The Directions apply to the following three amalgamation cases:

1. An NBFC merging with another NBFC.  
2. An NBFC merging with any entity that is **not** under the RBI’s regulatory purview.  
3. Any entity that is **not** under the RBI’s regulatory purview merging with an NBFC.  

These three scenarios are expressly listed in the Directions [S1].

items.question: NBFC ko apni digital payment architecture ko majboot aur scalable kaise banana chahiye aur IT security architecture ka periodic review board policy ke hisaab se kaise karna hai?
items.answer:
**डिजिटल पेमेंट आर्किटेक्चर को मजबूत और स्केलेबल बनाने के उपाय**

- NBFC को अपनी डिजिटल पेमेंट आर्किटेक्चर को लेन‑देन की वॉल्यूम और ग्राहक वृद्धि के अनुरूप मजबूत और स्केलेबल रखना है [S1]।  
- IT रणनीति में एक मजबूत कैपेसिटी मैनेजमेंट प्लान शामिल करना चाहिए ताकि बढ़ती डिमांड को पूरा किया जा सके [S1]।  
- नीति में क्षमता निर्माण और विस्तार (Scalability) को सुनिश्चित करते हुए ट्रांज़ैक्शन प्रोसेसिंग की कुशलता बढ़ाई जाए [S2‑(4)]।  
- उपलब्धता और हाई अवेलेबिलिटी के लिए इन्फ्रास्ट्रक्चर (मानव संसाधन और टेक्नोलॉजी) का बैक‑अप सुनिश्चित करें [S2‑(2)]।  
- सुरक्षा से संबंधित फ़ंक्शनल पॉइंट जैसे डेटा की गोपनीयता, इंटीग्रिटी और परफ़ॉर्मेंस को सुरक्षित तरीके से डिज़ाइन करें [S2‑(1‑3)]।  

**IT सिक्योरिटी आर्किटेक्चर का पिरियॉडिक रिव्यू कैसे करें**

- बोर्ड‑स्वीकृत नीति के अनुसार IT/IT सिक्योरिटी आर्किटेक्चर और टेक्नोलॉजी प्लेटफ़ॉर्म के ओवरहॉल के लिए एक मेकैनिज़्म स्थापित करें [S1]।  
- रिव्यू में नियमित (पिरियॉडिक) जांच शामिल होगी और यदि कोई आवश्यकता है तो त्वरित सुधारात्मक कार्रवाई की जाए [S1‑(3)]।  
- नीति में “उचित और समय‑सापेक्ष रिव्यू मैकेनिज़्म के साथ सही समय पर सुधारात्मक कार्रवाई” को स्पष्ट रूप से उल्लेख है [S2‑(7)]।  
- बोर्ड‑स्वीकृत IT/IS नीति में बेसिक सिक्योरिटी अस्पेक्ट्स जैसे फ़िज़िकल/लॉजिकल एक्सेस कंट्रोल, पासवर्ड पॉलिसी, मेकर‑चेकर कॉन्सेप्ट और रॉबस्ट साइबर सिक्योरिटी कंट्रोल शामिल हों [S4‑(1‑4)]।  
- रिव्यू रिपोर्ट को बोर्ड को कम से कम एक बार प्रति वर्ष प्रस्तुत करें ताकि ओवरसाइट सुनिश्चित हो [S4‑(8)]।  

इन बिंदुओं को अपनी डिजिटल पेमेंट नीति में शामिल कर NBFC अपनी आर्किटेक्चर को मजबूत, स्केलेबल और नियमित रिव्यू के साथ सुरक्षित रख सकेगा।

items.question: What approvals or clearances must be secured before the financial closure of a project financed by an NBFC?
items.answer:
All approvals or clearances that are **applicable to the implementation or construction of the project** must be obtained before financial closure. This includes, where relevant, environmental clearance, legal clearance, regulatory clearances, etc. [S1]

Approvals that are **contingent on the achievement of later project‑completion milestones** (e.g., consent to operate a boiler, which can only be applied for after the boiler is built) are not treated as mandatory pre‑requisite approvals at the time of financial closure; they become applicable only when the respective milestones are reached. [S2]

These four categories constitute the Large Exposure reporting requirements for an NBFC.

items.question: What conditions cause an asset to be classified as a non‑performing asset for a NBFC‑Middle Layer?
items.answer:
**An asset is classified as a non‑performing asset (NPA) for a NBFC‑Middle Layer when any one of the following conditions is met** [S1]:

1. Interest on the asset has remained overdue for **more than 90 days**.  
2. A term loan (including unpaid interest) where the instalment is overdue **more than 90 days** or the interest amount is overdue **more than 90 days**.  
3. A demand or call loan that is overdue **more than 90 days** from the date of demand or call, or whose interest amount is overdue **more than 90 days**.  
4. A bill that remains overdue **more than 90 days**.  
5. Interest on a debt or income on receivables under “other current assets” (short‑term loans/advances) where the facility is overdue **more than 90 days**.  
6. Any dues arising from the sale of assets, services rendered, or reimbursement of expenses that are overdue **more than 90 days**.  
7. Lease rental or hire‑purchase instalment that has become overdue **more than 90 days** (NBFC‑ML must classify each such account based on its record of recovery).  
8. The balance outstanding (including accrued interest) on loans, advances, or other credit facilities (including bills purchased/discounted) made available to the same borrower/beneficiary **when any of the above credit facilities becomes an NPA**.  

These eight criteria determine when an asset is treated as non‑performing for a NBFC‑Middle Layer.
